cards.text: Meet Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi. He's living among the exiles by the River Kebar, in the land of the Chaldeans, in the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile. And on the fifth day of the fourth month, the heavens open.

cards.question: The heavens open over the River Kebar. What does Ezekiel say he saw?
True or false: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel through another prophet.

cards.text: The word comes to him directly, and right there by the river, the LORD's hand is upon him. Then Ezekiel looks and sees a whirlwind coming from the north, a great cloud with brilliant light all around it.

cards.question: Inside that great cloud from the north, ___ is flashing back and forth.

cards.text: In the center of the fire is a gleam like amber, and within it, the form of four living creatures. Friend, a moth flew into my oven light ONE time and I had to go sit down.

cards.question: True or false: The four living creatures Ezekiel sees have a human form.

cards.text: A human form, yes. But each one has four faces and four wings, and the soles of their feet are like a calf's hooves, gleaming like polished bronze.

cards.question: Under their wings, on all four sides, the living creatures have human ___.

cards.text: Their wings are touching one another as they go. So four creatures, four faces each, wing to wing. How do they change direction?

cards.question: True or false: The living creatures turn as they move.

cards.text: No turning. Each one just goes straight ahead, and me? I need three tries and a backup camera just to get out of a parking spot.

cards.question: Each living creature has the face of a man. What are its other three faces?

cards.text: Their wings are spread upward. Each creature has two wings touching the wings of the creature on either side, and two wings covering its body.

cards.question: The living creatures never turn as they move. So what decides where they go?

cards.text: In the middle of the creatures is something that looks like glowing coals of fire, or torches. The fire moves back and forth between them, bright, with lightning flashing out of it.

cards.question: How fast are the living creatures darting back and forth?

answers.text: As quick as flashes of lightning
As quick as a running deer
As quick as a falling star

cards.text: Ezekiel keeps looking at the living creatures, each one with its four faces. Then he notices something on the ground beside each one.

cards.question: What does Ezekiel see on the ground beside each living creature?

cards.text: All four wheels look alike, gleaming like beryl. And their workmanship looks like a wheel within a wheel.

cards.question: True or false: The wheels can go in any of the four directions without pivoting.

cards.text: Their rims are high and awesome, and all four rims are full of eyes all around. That is more eyes than a whole street full of doorbell cameras.

cards.question: True or false: When the living creatures rise from the ground, the wheels stay on the ground.
The wheels rise right along with the living creatures. Why?

answers.text: The spirit of the creatures is in the wheels
The wheels are fastened to the creatures' feet
The creatures lift the wheels with their hands

cards.text: The creatures move, the wheels move. They stand still, the wheels stand still. Friend, I can't get one room of people to clap on the same beat.
Now Ezekiel's eyes go up, above the heads of the living creatures.

cards.question: What's spread out above the heads of the living creatures?

answers.text: An awesome expanse gleaming like crystal
A dark cloud filled with smoke
A tent made of blue linen

cards.text: Under the expanse, their wings stretch out toward one another. When they move, Ezekiel hears their wings like the roar of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the tumult of an army.

cards.question: True or false: When the living creatures stand still, they lower their wings.

cards.text: And while they stand still with their wings lowered, a voice comes from above the expanse over their heads.

cards.question: Above the expanse is the likeness of a ___ with the appearance of sapphire.
On the throne high above the expanse, what does Ezekiel see?

answers.text: A figure like that of a man
A figure like that of a lion
A figure like that of an eagle

cards.text: From what seemed to be His waist up, Ezekiel sees a gleam like amber with what looked like fire within it. From what seemed to be His waist down, what looked like fire, and brilliant light all around Him.

cards.question: The brilliant light all around Him looks like a ___ in a cloud on a rainy day.

cards.text: Then Ezekiel tells us what all of this is: "This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD." Read that line slow, friend, because every word in it is doing heavy lifting.

cards.question: Ezekiel sees the likeness of the glory of the LORD. What does he do?

answers.text: He runs back to the exiles
He shields his eyes and backs away

cards.text: Facedown on the ground, Ezekiel hears a voice speaking. And that's right where we'll stop for now, friend, because this story is far from done.

findings.problem: King Jehoiachin is named for the first time with no word on who he is. The card says only 'King Jehoiachin's exile.' It should say simply who he is, such as king of Judah. The card is already at its 3-sentence limit, so the fix has to fit inside those 3 sentences.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Their wings are touching one another as they go.' / 'So four creatures, four faces each, wing to wing.' / 'How do they change direction?' Story cards after the opening card can only have 1 to 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke gives Papa Dorin a new life detail outside his world. It has him driving a car with a backup camera and backing out of parking spots. He is a stamper on a gold base on a cookie planet. His jokes can only make up small moments and habits around his bakery. A comparison that doesn't claim he drives would keep the same idea of needing several tries to change direction.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'Then Ezekiel tells us what all of this is' goes beyond the text. Ezekiel 1:28 says 'This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD' right after it describes the brilliant light around the figure on the throne. The verse doesn't say whether 'This' covers the creatures, the wheels and the whole vision. Saying 'all of this' decides a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out because it is much shorter than the others. 'He falls facedown' has 3 words. 'He runs back to the exiles' has 6 and 'He shields his eyes and backs away' has 7.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
